Upload your own

Uploaded backgrounds stay on your device — other players still see the same board state and cards, just against their own choice of background.

What to notice
  • The room code is the entire security model — no accounts, no sign-up, nothing stored on a server.
  • Once a friend joins, their connection is direct to the host; the lobby just shows connection status.
  • "Connecting…" covers the one-time handshake through the public broker, described in DESIGN.md §3.
What to notice
  • Search runs against a card catalog cached on your device — no live API call per keystroke.
  • Click any card to open the same inspector used on the table — full art, oracle text, and keywords.
  • There's no legality checker — count and colors are shown for reference, not enforced.
What to notice
  • Every player's battlefield is visible, scaled down for opponents — only hands and libraries stay hidden.
  • Each board splits into four quadrants (creatures, planeswalkers, lands, artifacts & other); an empty quadrant just disappears, as with the "Planeswalkers" box on Sam and Jess's boards.
  • Identical, identically-tapped permanents collapse into one tile with a ×N badge — the nine Islands, for instance — but Grave Titan splits out on its own the moment it's tapped.
  • Click any card, anywhere, to inspect it full-size with its printed text and keywords. The ⋮ button is the separate tap/counter/move action menu.
  • Library, graveyard and exile are now small counters tucked next to the hand instead of large boxes.
What to notice
  • Default playmats are drawn with CSS gradients — no external images, so nothing to license.
  • An uploaded playmat is local-only in v1; syncing it to the table is a listed future enhancement.
  • Player color is just an identity cue used for avatars and life-total chips around the table.
